content.text: Localized collection of pus in breast tissue
MC in lactating women secondary to nipple trauma (esp. primigravida)
unilateral breast pain (esp. one quadrant) w/ tenderness, warmth, swelling, fever
cracked nipples or visible fissure + induration and fluctuance (due to pus)
– if question of cellulitis vs. abscess;
ill-defined mass w/ septations if abscess
Drainage via needle aspiration (lactational abscess) or I&D + abx
*not a contraindication to breast feeding – milk drainage is important to facilitate resolution of infection
Benign solid tumor composed of glandular & fibrous tissue
MC benign breast mass (after fibrocystic dz) & MC benign tumor in women <30yrs
but may become tender prior to menstruation
– most small tumors resorb w/ time
: may be needed if enlarging after repeat U/S or for large masses
Noncancerous, fluid-filled breast cysts due to exaggerated response to hormones
– duct dilation, breast cysts, & stromal fibrosis
*MC benign breast disorder in reproductive age women (esp. 30-50yrs)
may ↑ or ↓ in size w/ menstrual hormonal changes
, nodular, mobile, smooth round or ovoid lumps in both breasts of varying sizes
& usually NOT associated w/ axillary lymph node involvement
MC found in upper outer sections of the breast
– test of choice; dense, prominent, fibroglandular tissue w/ cysts but no discernable mass
dry aspirate, blood aspirate, persistent/recurrent mass after aspirate
: observation, supportive bra, low fat diet, reduce caffeine & chocolate intake, warm/cool compress, analgesics, evening primrose oil or vitamin E
*FNA removal or fluid is diagnostic & therapeutic in complex cases
Infection of the breast MC in lactating women secondary to nipple trauma (esp. primigravida in the first 6wks postpartum)
unilateral localized breast pain, tenderness, warmth, swelling, induration, & skin redness
Culture of breast milk – for sensitivities
Imaging – reserved for cases not responding to empiric abx within 48-72hrs
: warm/cool compresses, breast pump, anti-inflammatory medications
•erythromycin can be used in PCN allergy
*Mothers encouraged to continue breastfeeding – milk drainage is critical for resolution of infection & relief of sxs
